title: Improved Bounds on Diffsequences with Gaps in Powers of 2: the improved lower bound for $\Delta(D,k)$ (Theorem 1)
author: Kanav Talwar and Utkarsh Gupta
work: Improved Bounds on Diffsequences with Gaps in Powers of 2
difficulty_reason: Counted unit: the paper's improved lower bound for Delta(D,k) for the set D of powers of two, printed as Theorem 1 (source0.tex lines 175--180), delivered together with the paper's own complete proof of it at source0.tex lines 365--372. The preparation note for this item reported that the main theorem has no adjacent proof, and that is correct: the proof is detached. It is, however, present and complete. After the proof of Lemma 1 the paper opens a run-in block headed Proof of Theorem 1 and proves the theorem there in one paragraph plus one displayed equation plus one closing paragraph, and that block is the only proof of the counted theorem anywhere in the paper. The proof's structure is as follows. It fixes the alternating binary string of length l and recalls that its whole index sequence is a diffsequence with l-1 hops, so that psi of that string at l-1 hops equals l. It then instantiates Lemma 1, whose statement is psi_{s^(1)}(h) <= psi_s(h+1) + 3h + 2, along the chain of successive expansions with h = l-1-i, obtaining one inequality for each i from 1 to l-1. Summing those l-1 inequalities telescopes the psi terms and leaves a constant term that is the sum of the arithmetic progression 3(l-i-1)+2; the display evaluates it to l + 3(l-1)(l-2)/2 + 2(l-1) = (3l^2-3l+2)/2. Since a colouring of length l times 4^(l-1) then admits no monochromatic diffsequence of length k for every k greater than (3l^2-3l+2)/2, the paper concludes Delta(D,k) >= l times 4^(l-1), and finally chooses the largest admissible l by inverting the quadratic, l = floor( sqrt( 2(k-1)/3 + 1/4 ) + 1/2 ), which turns the bound into the closed form displayed in the counted statement. The block is short in line count, but its substance is not: everything rests on the paper's own hop-counting lemma, whose proof is an induction that splits a diffsequence at its first hop, applies the two corollaries of Proposition 1 to the two parts, and tracks the at most three indices lost per step; the summation step and the optimisation of l over the integers are the paper's own contributions, and the resulting bound improves the exponential constant of Clifton's published bound from sqrt(2k) to sqrt(8k/3). The paper's other proved statements are weaker units: Proposition 1 has a five-line case analysis, Corollaries 1 and 2 have three-line proofs, and Lemma 1, which is the real engine of the paper, has a five-line proof and is a lemma rather than the main result. Counting the main theorem together with its complete detached proof is therefore the strongest unit the paper offers. For an honest statement of what a solver must supply: the definition of the expansion, position and hop machinery, the two corollaries and the lemma must be available, and even then the argument has to be carried out, since it is the paper's research contribution and not a textbook exercise. That places the unit in the upper qualifying-to-research range: H2. The counted proof is delivered exactly as the paper wrote it, including its run-in bold heading.
